title: hybrid-routing-quota-drift-silent-rejections
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported sudden unexplained request rejections over the past 72 hours. Symptoms included elevated 429/opaque-denial rates from edge proxies, console quota UIs showing rapid consumption without corresponding traffic spikes, and degraded tail-latency for routed requests. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix for a token-bucket state-drift issue exposed by our hybrid routing logic between Hosted and Dedicated routing layers.
timeline: 2026-02-27: First alert from monitoring (unexpected quota depletion for 3 Hosted tenants). 2026-02-28: Dedicated customer support ticket and escalations from two large customers experiencing intermittent rejections. 2026-02-29: On-call identified desynced rate-limiter state during cross-region failover; temporary mitigations applied. 2026-03-01: Ticket created to track permanent fixes and rollout plan.
impact_details: Affected: ~6 customers (mix of Hosted and Dedicated), several internal prod routes. User-visible: 10-30% request rejection spikes for impacted tenants, increased latencies due to retry storms. Business: one customer opened an escalation citing production outage. Root cause appears to cause silent quota exhaustion where gateway and cluster-local rate-limiter disagree on available tokens.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token-bucket decay math divergence across rate-limiter replicas combined with hybrid routing path selection (requests bouncing between Hosted edge and Dedicated egress) led to double-accounting or stale credits. Key signals: 1) Timestamp skew between nodes (~700ms in one Dedicated cluster). 2) Inconsistent serialization format (legacy v1 vs v2) of bucket state during migration; older replicas occasionally ignored remote reconciliations. 3) A routing optimization introduced in Jan routing release cause sticky session bypass for some flows, exposing the mismatch more frequently.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a Dedicated cluster with mixed v1/v2 limiter replicas. 2) Configure a tenant with low burst allowance and enable hybrid routing to Hosted fallback. 3) Send sustained moderate QPS with periodic spikes; observe console quota drop without matching request counts and gate-level rejects. Reproducible in staging with the provided repro harness link.
mitigations_applied: - Immediate: Enabled conservative fallback policy to allow Hosted-only routing for impacted tenants (reduced cross-cluster routing) to stop mismatch-induced rejections. - Short-term: Rolled out patch that enforces TTL-based local credit refresh on replicas to surface stale state as a temporary permissive mode. - Communication: Notified affected customers and posted incident status in status.redwood.com and internal Slack incident channel.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Normalize token-bucket serialization to a single canonical schema (v3) and full schema migration with backward compatibility checks. 2) Implement stronger reconciliation protocol: versioned state + monotonic vector and safe merge rules. 3) Add cross-cluster distributed clock guard and monotonic timestamp enforcement to avoid decay skew. 4) Remove routing optimization path that bypasses local limiter for sticky sessions until reconciliation proven resilient. 5) Add end-to-end tests in the routing+limiter matrix and a chaos test for clock skew.
implementation_notes: - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1148 (token-bucket-v3 + reconciliation protocol) - Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Token+Bucket+Reconciliation+Design - Staging repro harness: https://staging.redwood.ai/repro/hybrid-quota-drift - Feature flag: limiter.v3_migration gated by 'limit-v3-migrate' flag per-cluster.
testing_plan: - Unit: serialization roundtrip, merge idempotency, monotonic timestamp tests. - Integration: cluster-local and cross-cluster reconciliation on staging with simulated network partitions and clock skews. - Load: run ramp from 0->peak on staging and measure acceptance ratios vs expected token consumption. - Canaries: progressive rollout to 10% Hosted tenants, then 50%, monitor console and SLO dashboards for 24h windows.
rollout_steps: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging clusters and run test harness (2 days). 3) Canary deploy to one non-critical Hosted region + one small Dedicated customer (48h observation). 4) If metrics stable, expand to remaining Hosted regions and Dedicated clusters incrementally. 5) Post-rollout: trigger forced reconciliation window and drain legacy replicas after 7 days.
rollback_plan: Disable feature flag and re-enable conservative fallback routing. If immediate disable does not restore normal behavior, revert the last routing optimization change and restore previous token refresh TTLs. Rollback playbook available at: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quota+Rollback+Playbook
postmortem_actions: - Complete schema migration and removal of legacy serialization within 30 days. - Add runbook entries for cross-cluster quota incidents and include automated reconciliation check in weekly health jobs. - Deliver a customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit evaluation with CS. - Add observability: per-tenant reconciliation mismatch metric and alert with P99 thresholds.
